issues.legal_issue: The age and existing condition of a building are relevant, but not conclusive, factors in assessing a landlord’s bona fide requirement for demolition and reconstruction.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction for demolition and reconstruction, relying on an honest intention, sufficient funds, and approved plans.
The building was more than 70 years old, but the evidence included a municipal notice requiring specified repairs, and the building’s condition was disputed.
The lower courts treated the building’s age and condition as irrelevant to the landlord’s bona fide requirement.
The enactment provided for the tenant’s return if the landlord failed to demolish as undertaken, but did not provide for the tenant’s reinduction into the reconstructed building.
issues.conclusion: The building’s age and existing condition cannot be ignored; they form part of all the circumstances relevant to bona fide requirement, though neither old age nor dilapidation is a necessary or decisive condition for eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14(1)(b) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, the Controller assesses whether the building is bona fide required for immediate demolition and reconstruction by considering all surrounding circumstances, including the building’s age, condition and situation, the landlord’s means and steps toward reconstruction, and the prospect of more profitable use after reconstruction. Sections 14(2)(b) and 16 provide for the landlord’s undertaking and the tenant’s return if demolition is not carried out as undertaken; the absence of a right to reoccupy the reconstructed building may affect the weight given to the building’s condition. Neta Ram v. Jiwan Lal and Mehsin Bhai v. Hale & Company were approved. Panchamal Narayan Shenoy v. Basthi Venkatesha Shenoy was distinguished in light of the different statutory scheme, including its provision for reoccupation of the reconstructed building; S. M. Gopalakrishna Chetty v. Ganeshan was distinguished as addressing a different issue.

predicates.demolition_reconstruction_eviction_proce: A landlord seeks eviction of a tenant so that the building can be demolished and reconstructed.
predicates.landlord_bona_fide_requirement_is_under_: The decision-maker is assessing whether the landlord genuinely requires the building for demolition and reconstruction.

issues.definition: When a demolition-and-reconstruction eviction proceeding requires assessment of the landlord’s genuine requirement, the building’s age and condition are relevant factors.

issues.legal_issue: An eviction determination must be reconsidered when the decision-makers assess bona fide requirement for demolition and reconstruction while wholly ignoring the building’s existing condition.
material_facts: The tenants challenged eviction orders based on the landlord’s claimed requirement for demolition and reconstruction.
The lower courts relied on the landlord’s intention, funds, and steps toward reconstruction but did not consider the building’s existing condition.
The Supreme Court set aside the lower courts’ conclusions and returned the applications for reconsideration.
issues.conclusion: The conclusions on bona fide requirement were set aside, and the landlord’s applications were remanded to the Rent Controller for disposal in light of the judgment.
issues.legal_principle: The existing condition of the building is a vital factor within the circumstances to be considered under section 14(1)(b) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960. A determination that wholly ignores that factor cannot stand. The Court relied on the principles in Neta Ram v. Jiwan Lal and Mehsin Bhai v. Hale & Company.

predicates.tenant_appeal_from_demolition_reconstruc: A tenant appeals an eviction determination made on the ground that the landlord requires demolition and reconstruction.
predicates.lower_decision_ignored_building_conditio: The decision-makers assessing the landlord’s genuine requirement did not consider the building’s existing condition.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals a demolition-and-reconstruction eviction determination and the lower decision ignored the building’s condition, the eviction finding is set aside and the application is remanded.
